Decision — one system binary

Status: accepted 2026-10-12. Amends the source layout (AGENTS.md §2.3, §3.4, §6 and §9).

The decision

  • One binary, mix, carries the shell and every headless daemon. It is built by a new host component, cli/system (package system, kind cli). The host's only code is the dispatcher and the global allocator.
  • A daemon is a personality, chosen by the name the binary was started as. noded, maild, webd and the rest are symlinks to mix in /opt/mixos/bin. Each still runs as its own process, under its own unit and journal identity, because the kernel names a process after the name it was executed by. There are no daemon subcommands under mix: the shell's first-argument namespace stays the shell's.
    • mix --personalities lists what the binary contains, with each component's version.
    • An unknown name exits 2 and prints that list.
    • The shell's self re-execution passes mix as its name, so a re-exec from a daemon personality comes back as the shell.
  • Components keep their identity. Each daemon keeps its own crate, tests, units, metadata, version and verb registry. Its library exports pub fn main() -> ExitCode; its own [[bin]] stays for development builds. cli/mix-shell becomes a library with no binary.
  • What goes in: the shell, noded, and every headless base and server daemon as it arrives, including the headless desktop-profile services. What stays out: anything with a GUI stack (compd, the applications), and any daemon whose dependencies dwarf the rest. The install-profile gate's closure check enforces the first.
  • One personality per process. No setup happens at link or load time. The async runtime, TLS provider, signal masks, panic hook and logger are set up in the personality's own main, never in a shared library's initialiser. Each personality passes its own logging identity and records its own build provenance. Every personality uses one allocator, mimalloc. A test starts every personality and checks its identity.
  • Fleet builds are static. The shipped binary targets x86_64-unknown-linux-musl, fully static, so one file runs on every supported distribution regardless of its C library.
  • Shell tests test the shipped binary. The shell's process-level tests live in cli/system/tests/ and run mix as built by the host.

Why

Every daemon links the same core: the async runtime, serialisation, the Bus, the Mix evaluator, logging. Linked separately, each carries its own copy, and every release links that core once per daemon. Measured on the first two-personality build (the shell and noded), the combined binary was 11% smaller than the two separate ones and its release link took 40% less time. Both gains grow with each personality. A static musl build cost nothing in size, startup or evaluator speed, and the same file ran on both distributions tested.

One file also means one artifact per architecture, one hash to verify and one version on every node. Running daemons keep the old file's inode, so an upgrade restarts only the units whose component changed.

Memory is not part of the case: different personalities run different code, so they share little.

Consequences

  • AGENTS.md §2.3: cli/system builds the mix binary. cli/mix-shell is the shell's library and builds no binary.
  • AGENTS.md §3.4: a daemon may be installed as a personality, a symlink named after its component; units name the symlink.
  • AGENTS.md §6: cli/system is the one package allowed a non-dev dependency on kind = "cli" packages.
  • AGENTS.md §9: the bootstrap is cargo build --profile release-fast -p system.
  • Build scripts that built -p mix-shell to get mix build -p system.
  • The installer creates each node's personality symlinks from its install profiles, keeps the previous binary for rollback, and restarts only changed units. The release archive's manifest lists each personality with its component version.
